title: Chronicle: token-slice observability and billing bridge
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Build an end-to-end observability pipeline that produces high-fidelity token-level timing slices and a deterministic billing bridge. This ticket targets three deliverables: (1) instrument the serving runtime to emit compact per-token slice spans that include kernel stage, queue wait, KV cache decision and hit/miss flags; (2) enrich the metrics/log pipeline to correlate slices with request-level traces and cost models; (3) provide dashboards and a billing-export-ready artifact that translates slices into chargeable units for accounting and customer-facing insights. Motivation: current tracing is coarse (request-level + high-level phases) which obscures KV cache economics and micro-latency hotspots. The new signals should enable accurate cache chargebacks, SLA debugging, and more precise cost optimization suggestions in Redwood Optimize.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits a compact 'token_slice' span for every emitted token with fields: token_index, stage (embed/attend/kv/emit), start_ts, end_ts, kv_decision: {checked|skipped|hit|miss}, kernel_hint, thread_id, and request_id.
Tracing pipeline ingests token_slice spans and stitches them to parent request traces with <100ms processing lag in staging and <1s in production sampling tier.
A canonical map from token_slice attributes to billing units exists and is validated by a reconciliation job that matches sample traces to invoiced tokens within 2% over a week-long sample.
New Grafana dashboards show per-model and per-route distributions: token latency histogram, KV hit-rate by prefix length, tail-latency attribution by stage, and cost-per-token breakdown.
No P99 latency regression for the baseline API under synthetic load (+/- 5%); resource overhead from instrumentation remains <8% CPU and <4% memory on serving nodes in staging.
Documentation updated (Confluence link) with data contract, field definitions, retention, and migration notes for downstream consumers (billing, alerts, Optimize engine).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (runtime): add lightweight token_slice emission inside the emitter loop. Use packed protobuf-lite event to minimize allocations. Gate by sampling flag and a runtime feature toggle.
Phase 2 (ingest): extend Jaeger/OTLP collector pipeline with a token_slice normalizer that flattens the packed fields and emits a token_slice metric stream to ClickHouse + traces to the trace index.

Phase 3 (billing bridge): implement a reconciliation microservice that consumes enriched token slices, applies the pricing map (model, quantization, kernel_hint), and emits per-request cost items to Billing S3 exporter.
Phase 4 (dashboards): author Grafana panels and pre-computed rollups in ClickHouse for percentiles and per-route cost breakdowns. Add drilldowns from request trace to token_slice timeline.
Phase 5 (QA & rollout): staged rollout with sampling 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> default for Dedicated customers; monitor overhead and error surface.
testing_plan: Unit tests for token_slice serializer/deserializer and sampling toggle behaviors.
Load test in perf cluster with synthetic LLM workloads to measure instrumentation overhead at 1%, 5%, and 100% sampling.
End-to-end integration test: synthetic traces ingested -> stitched -> reconciled -> billing export validated against a golden dataset.
Chaos test: simulate KV cache flaps and verify token_slice kv_decision flags and downstream reconcilers handle transient inconsistencies.
Privacy check: ensure token values are never emitted; only token_index/length and non-sensitive flags are present.
rollout_plan: Feature toggle controls runtime emission; default off for all existing tenants.
Enable 0.1% global sampling in staging for 48 hours and validate ingestion correctness and storage impact.
Progressively increase sampling and enable for specific high-usage Dedicated customers (opt-in) to gather operational feedback.
Flip default on for internal telemetry only (no billing) once P95 cost mapping validated; then enable billing bridge for pilot accounts.
Deprecation: keep legacy coarse trace fields for 90 days post-rollout, with migration docs for downstream consumers.

metrics_queries:
-- ClickHouse: token slice latency distribution by model
SELECT model, quantile(0.5)(duration_ms), quantile(0.95)(duration_ms), quantile(0.99)(duration_ms) FROM token_slices WHERE timestamp >= today()-7 GROUP BY model

-- KV hit-rate by prefix length (approx)
SELECT model, prefix_len, avg(kv_hit) FROM token_slices WHERE timestamp >= yesterday() GROUP BY model, prefix_len

-- Cost reconciliation summary
SELECT sum(estimated_cost_usd) as reconcile_cost, countDistinct(request_id) as requests FROM billing_items WHERE window = 'weekly'

-- Tail attribution: top N routes contributing to P99 token latency
SELECT route, quantile(0.99)(duration_ms) as p99 FROM token_slices WHERE timestamp >= today()-14 GROUP BY route ORDER BY p99 DESC LIMIT 25
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Instrumentation overhead causes tail regressions under peak load. Mitigation: sampling gated by toggle, implement pooled buffers, roll out incrementally and monitor P99 closely.
Risk: High cardinality in token_slice fields (e.g., kernel_hint variants) increases storage costs. Mitigation: canonicalize kernel_hint values, map to small enumerations, and compress before writing.

Risk: Downstream billing consumers interpret slices differently leading to invoice drift. Mitigation: implement deterministic reconciliation job and weekly reconciliation reports; require billing sign-off before customer-facing billing.
Risk: Privacy exposure. Mitigation: explicit schema that excludes token bytes; automated tests and a security gating job prior to prod enablement.
